newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Petrobras in $800 mln refinery study.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Petrobras in $800 mln refinery study.

text.p: Brazilian state oil giant Petrobras and private petrochemical firm Copene are signing a letter of intent today to study the viability of building an $800 million refinery in northeastern Brazil, a Petrobras spokeswoman said.
She said this would be the first refinery to be built in partnership with the private sector since Petrobras' monopoly of the Brazilian oil and gas sector was established in 1953.

"This is only a letter of intent in anticipation of new legislation opening the Brazilian oil sector to private capital," she said. "Under current legislation Petrobras could not build the refinery in partnership with a private company."
The plant to be built near Salvador in the state of Bahia would produce naphtha and fuel oil which would be used in Copene's primary resource center in Camacari, Bahia.
Copene supplies raw material to the Camacari petrochemical complex and has been studying the project with an eye toward becoming self-sufficient in naphtha.
